children: Bodycote agreed to an improved  takeover proposal from Veritas Capital, valuing it at around 1.64 billion pounds ($2.22 billion) including debt, though rival private-equity suitor CVC Advisers urged shareholders to take no action.

Under the terms of the Veritas proposal, Bodycote shareholders will be entitled to receive 940 pence for each share held. This comprises 932.8 pence in cash per share as well as a 7.2 pence interim dividend.

Bodycote said the 932.8 pence cash offer, not including the dividend, reflected a 36.5% premium to its three-month volume-weighted average share price of 683.4 pence prior to May 22, when the company said it was in talks with Apollo Management regarding a 1.52 billion-pound takeover proposal.
"The board remains highly confident in Bodycote's prospects and believes that this offer recognizes that value today and is therefore recommending it to shareholders," Chairman Daniel Dayan said.

In August,  Bodycote said it had received offers from both Veritas and CVC. The CVC offer of 915 pence a share implied an equity valuation of around 1.56 billion pounds, while the Veritas proposal was for 914 pence a share.
CVC Advisers said Tuesday that it was considering its position and urged Bodycote shareholders to take no action in response to the Veritas offer in the meantime.
In early trading, London-listed Bodycote shares were up 4.5% at 954 pence, and are up 50% over the past 12 months.
